messages:
mike: Heads-up 1: we keep getting asks to fast-track non-critical improvements for named customers. Proposing a small "customer-exception" lane so CS can request expedited handling with documented criteria.

anya: curious how this differs from Tier-A SLA. Are we creating another exception band?

mike: Good q. Tier-A is contractual. This lane is for ad-hoc commercial asks (one-off revenue-impact requests) that don't change the roadmap but need faster turnaround. It should have strict gates so it doesn't eat roadmap.

kevin: From eng: fine if we cap it. Suggest rules: 1) max 2 exceptions active per sprint; 2) each exception <= 5 dev-days; 3) must include a rollback plan & ff.

julia: CS/process note: requests must include an approved "expedite" chit signed by CS lead + RevOps rep. We'll only accept if revenue delta > $X or critical legal/regulatory need.

pat: Telemetry/ops: we should require a short impact signal (e.g., repro + metric link). I'll attach a template for the PD/Grafana snippet so triage has data.

mike: Proposed intake template for exception lane:
```
- customer: name + contact
- revenue-impact: $ or escalation rationale
- request: what to change
- quick-repro: steps + telemetry link
- dev-est: 1-line
- owner: CS & squad
- expedite-approval: CS-lead + RevOps email
```

anya: Love the template. For governance: exceptions expire after 30 days unless renewed with another chit. Also require a post-delivery note to the customer with roll-forward/back plan.

kevin: Operational constraints: we reserve 15% of sprint capacity for exceptions for next 2 sprints, after that reevaluate. Exceptions that sum >15% -> auto-deny unless exec sign-off.

julia: I'll own the approval flow + RevOps sign-off. We'll build a simple Google Form that writes to the tracker. CS should not DM requests.

pat: I'll provide a Grafana quick-link macro so CS pastes the signal into the ticket. Also add a PD escalation that mentions "customer-exception" in the alert so triage sees it.

mike: Rollout rules: 1) feature-flag or toggle is mandatory; 2) canary at min 5% for 6h; 3) smoke checks + manual approval to full rollout. If no ff possible, require a DB migration reversal plan.

kevin: If the exception touches model-serving/runtime paths, require an extra perf-test sign-off from eng-runtime. No exceptions there without runtime sign-off.

anya: For customer comms: CS will send a templated message: expected initial response in 4h, ETA for dev work in 48h, and a follow-up plan. We'll include the rollback paragraph.

julia: Action items: 1) julia -> build approval form + RevOps workflow by Wed. 2) kevin -> exception capacity cap + quick-est template in issue templates. 3) pat -> Grafana macro + PD tag. 4) mike -> add one-pager to handbook and create tracker. I'll sync Thurs 10:00 to ratify wording.

julia: Confirmed. Form will include required CS-lead and RevOps sign-off fields.

kevin: Confirmed. I'll also add an automation: if exception approvals >2 in a given week, alert PM leads.

pat: Confirmed. Macro link will be posted here when ready.

mike: One small edge-case: what about legal/regulatory asks on customer infra? Those should bypass the exception lane and go straight to legal + eng-ops. We'll note that in the one-pager.

anya: Good call. Add that.

mike: Anything blocking?

julia: No blockers from RevOps.

kevin: No blockers from eng, but please keep the cap firm.

pat: No blockers.

mike: OK closing loop 1. I'll drop the one-pager here after Thurs sync and create the tracker link. If you spot missing checks, drop them into this thread.

cs-bot: Reminder: use CS intake template for formal requests: https://redwood.internal/cs/exception-intake (auto-post)

deploy-bot: Runbook link for rollbacks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-playbook (auto-post)
